title: NEMAR Zarr serving index (format_version 3)
description: The mandatory entry point to a dataset's Zarr serving copy at <data_base>index.json. Anonymous ListBucket is denied on the serving bucket, so this document -- not a listing -- is how a client discovers what is served, where to read it from, and why a recording is missing. Produced by scripts/zarr/generate_zarr.py (nemarOrg/nemar-cli); consumed by nemar.org, the backend catalog sweep, and external clients. contract_base is the only URL a client may hardcode: data_base / s3_uri describe where the bytes happen to live today and may change per dataset.

contract_base.description: The STABLE base URL for this dataset's serving copy (https://<zarr host>/<id>/zarr/). The only base a client may hardcode.

data_base.description: Where the bytes are served from TODAY, for an HTTP Zarr reader. May change; re-read it from this document rather than hardcoding it.

data_base_kind.description: What kind of thing data_base points at, so a client knows which access pattern applies.

s3_uri.description: The same location as an s3:// triple, for boto3 / s3fs / zarr, which want bucket+key rather than a URL to parse back apart.

s3_anonymous.description: True when s3_uri is readable with unsigned requests (no credentials needed).

source_commit.description: The dataset repository commit this serving copy was built from. Always a full 40-hex SHA; the producer refuses to publish an index without one (#1197).

engine_version.description: The discovery/dispatch generation that produced this index (zarr_queue.ZARR_ENGINE_VERSION). Changes only when discovery widens; see ADR 0033.

biosigio_version.description: The biosigIO release that wrote the stores, or null when it could not be determined.

updated_utc.description: When this run wrote the index (UTC, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ).

discovered_count.description: Raw recordings the walker found at source_commit, after the ADR 0027 exclusions (derivatives/, sourcedata/, code/, BIDS MEG calibration files). The denominator of coverage. INVARIANT: discovered_count == store_count + failure_count + pending_count.

store_count.description: Recordings with a served store. Authoritative -- prefer it to stores.length.

n_recordings.description: Alias of store_count, kept for the #1059 field list. Not the discovered total; that is discovered_count.

errors.description: Recordings that failed in THIS run, typed and untyped alike. A run statistic, not a coverage total: the coverage totals are failure_count and pending_count, which carry across runs.

failure_count.description: Entries in failures[] -- recordings that will not convert without a change to the data or the converter.

pending_count.description: Entries in pending[] -- recordings with no store yet that are still expected to convert on a later run.

doi.description: Concept DOI for the dataset (the version DOI is per release, not per serving copy). Null when the catalog has none yet. Hoisted from the store attrs so a citation tool needs only this document.

license.description: Dataset license as the catalog states it. Null when unknown -- not 'no license'.

citation.description: Ready-to-paste citation composed from the catalog row. Null when the row lacks the parts to make one honestly.

hed_version.description: HED schema version the dataset's annotations use, or null.

events_parquet.description: URL of this dataset's events file, one Parquet row per (event, channel group) across every store (#1060). ABSENT means there is no file to read: the dataset has no events.tsv anywhere, or this run could not publish one -- never assume the path exists. Columns: store_path (joins to stores[].zarr), subject, session, task, run, onset_s, duration_s, sample_index, group_name, trial_type, value, hed, then the remaining events.tsv columns under their own names (x_-prefixed only on a collision with those). sample_index is the LEVEL-0 sample the onset falls on, computed by the converter -- which is the only party that knows the exact resampling relation -- so a client never re-derives it.

events_row_count.description: Rows in events_parquet. Present exactly when events_parquet is. NOT the event count: a store with two channel groups contributes two rows per event, one per group, because an onset lands on a different sample in each. The per-store event counts are stores[].n_events, produced by the same parse.

layout.description: How to turn this index's numbers into reads, so an MCP recipe (ADR 0025) is computable from index.json plus ONE array-metadata fetch, with no probing. Paths are relative to contract_base; <zarr> is a store's `zarr`, <group> a groups[].name, <L> a view level. `events` is the exception and is stated against data_base, because it is a single object rather than a store path and the index also publishes its URL directly as events_parquet -- which is what says whether it EXISTS. const values: a client may hardcode them once it has checked format_version, and changing the layout is therefore a schema change rather than a silent one.

scale_offset.const: level-0 array attrs scale[] and offset[]; physical = digital * scale + offset

store.description: One converted recording. Read the bytes at <contract_base><zarr>/.

path.description: The recording's path inside the BIDS dataset, relative to the repository root.

zarr.description: The store's path relative to contract_base / data_base.

source_tree.description: Which BIDS tree the SOURCE recording lives in. Always 'raw': ADR 0027 made discovery raw-only, and a carried-over store under derivatives/, sourcedata/ or code/ is DROPPED from the index rather than republished, because those stores are being deleted (scripts/zarr/purge_non_raw_stores.py), not served. The producer reports how many it dropped as non_raw_dropped on its callback. The field is stated rather than implied so a consumer never has to infer the tree from the path.

derived.description: True when the served signal is PROCESSED rather than the source signal quantized and rate-capped. Today the only true case is an ADR 0028 Signal-Space Separation MEG store, which also carries `sss`. Deliberately distinct from source_tree, which is about BIDS layout.

n_events.description: Rows in the events.tsv the converter applied. Absent when the recording has no applicable events.tsv (which is not the same as an empty one).

trial_types.description: Counts per trial_type value in that same events.tsv, so a client can pick an epoching strategy without reading a signal byte. A key is the value itself when it has 128 Unicode code points or fewer (not bytes or UTF-16 units; the value is stripped first). A longer value (some datasets store a whole record in the column for some recordings, so each of those events is distinct) is keyed by 28 characters instead: its first 13 code points, "~", and the first 14 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its UTF-8 bytes. Values that fit claim their own key first, then long values sorted by code point, and a long value whose key is already taken is re-hashed over the decimal salt n = 1, 2, ..., one NUL byte, and the value until its key is free, so a client can reproduce a salted key. Distinct values always have distinct keys and no counts are merged; the index still holds one key per distinct value, about 33 bytes for a long one instead of its whole length. The full value is in the trial_type column of events.parquet when events_parquet is listed. An index published before this rule carries the literal value for a longer one, so look up the literal value first and then its digest form. Absent when there is no events.tsv; an empty object means the file has no trial_type column, or every row is blank or n/a.

units_report.description: biosigIO's per-file account of what the BIDS channels.tsv `units` column did (biosigio#125), republished so a unit that could NOT be adopted is visible without opening the store. Absent when no channels.tsv was applied to the recording -- either the dataset ships none that inherits to it, or the sidecar could not be read. Never means "applied cleanly". Both the in-memory and the streaming exporter apply it (biosigio>=1.2.7), so the two cannot disagree about a recording's units.

sidecar.description: Repository-relative path of the channels.tsv the converter resolved (BIDS inheritance: the most specific applicable sidecar, which may live in an ancestor directory).

sidecar_supplied.description: True when the converter passed that sidecar to the exporter explicitly rather than relying on sibling auto-detection. Load-bearing for the ADR 0028 MaxShield path, where the exporter is handed a filtered copy in a scratch directory with no sidecar beside it.

unmatched_channels.description: Store channels no channels.tsv row reached, so the sidecar's type and unit were NOT applied to them and they carry the importer's. A row reaches the channel it names exactly and, from biosigio 1.2.10, the one channel whose label differs from it only in letter case when that match is unambiguous (counted in matched_case_only, not here). The counts above cover only matched rows, which is why this is reported separately. 0 means every channel met a row. Absent when there was no join to report on: the store records no channel labels, the channels.tsv has no name column, or there is no units_report at all (no channels.tsv applied); and on stores converted before the converter reported it.

unmatched_case_only.description: Of unmatched_channels, those a row names in a different letter case (EDF header FP1-F7, channels.tsv Fp1-F7) that were NOT matched: the store was converted with a biosigio before 1.2.10, which matched names exactly, or the case-insensitive match was ambiguous (two channels, or two rows, fold to the same name). Either way the sidecar's type and unit were not applied. Absent when there are none.

matched_case_only.description: Store channels a channels.tsv row reached only by ignoring letter case (EDF header FP1-F7, channels.tsv Fp1-F7; biosigio 1.2.10 and later). The sidecar's type and unit WERE applied to them, so a unit that differs from the file's was converted. Absent when there are none, and on stores converted before biosigio 1.2.10.

matched_case_only_examples.description: Up to five of the matched_case_only matches, each as "<channels.tsv name> -> <store channel label>", in channels.tsv row order. Present exactly when matched_case_only is.

matched_case_insensitive.description: Never published. biosigio's own report names every case-only match in a per-channel map under this key; the converter republishes it bounded, as matched_case_only and matched_case_only_examples, so an index entry does not grow with the channel count. Declared here so the converter's pre-upload check refuses an index that carries the map.

unmatched_raw_label.description: Of unmatched_channels, those whose file label was repeated and so de-duplicated in the store (T8-P8 twice becomes T8-P8-0 and T8-P8-1), while channels.tsv names the repeated label. Absent when there are none.

unmatched_examples.description: Up to five store labels among unmatched_channels, in store order. Present exactly when unmatched_channels is non-zero.

channels_tsv_read_error.description: True when a channels.tsv that APPLIES to this recording exists at source_commit but could not be read, so the store carries the importer's units rather than the sidecar's. Distinct from an absent units_report, which means the dataset ships no applicable sidecar at all.

channels_tsv_count_mismatch.description: Present when the recording's channels.tsv declares more channels than its data file holds. The store serves every channel the file's own header declares, so it is faithful to the data; the sidecar over-declares. A store short of the FILE is never published (channel_count_mismatch). Absent when the counts agree or no channels.tsv applies.

channels_tsv.description: Data rows in the applicable channels.tsv.

in_file.description: Data channels the recording file's own header declares, read without the importer (EDF/BDF signal count less the annotation track; BrainVision NumberOfChannels; FIF nchan; EEGLAB .set nbchan, used only where it equals the data matrix's rows).

in_store.description: Channels this store serves, summed across its groups.

split_members.description: Every source path of a split FIF chain served by this one store, so a click on split-02 resolves here.

sss.description: ADR 0028 Signal-Space Separation parameters, present exactly when derived is true.

group.description: One channel group inside a store (biosigIO names them <modality>_<rate>hz). Groups are concurrent streams of ONE recording: a store's duration is the max over its groups, never their sum.

rate.description: The SERVING rate after the NEMAR modality cap, not the acquisition rate. The acquisition rate is source_rate_hz (and the BIDS sidecar's SamplingFrequency).

source_rate_hz.description: The recording's own sampling rate before the cap (level-0 attr).

n_view_levels.description: How many view/* min-max envelope levels exist, so a reader never probes for them (#1178 item 2).

view_chunk_columns.description: Columns per view chunk -- constant across levels since biosigio 1.2.6, so a viewport-sized read is 1-3 requests at any level (#1178 item 1).

failure.description: A recording that has no store for a reason retrying will not change: a property of the data, or a converter gap someone has to close.

code.description: Stable machine code (biosigIO's own, plus the NEMAR-side recording_too_large / channel_count_mismatch / maxshield_uncalibrated / maxshield_probe_failed / fdt_declaration_refused / annex_object_missing / companion_missing / split_part_missing / epoched_recording / retry_exhausted).

reason.description: The sanitized, user-facing sentence the viewer shows. Never a raw exception.

detail.description: Operator-facing cause: the exception class plus the first line of its message, with local filesystem paths stripped. This is what makes an opaque file_read_error diagnosable from the public index (#1197).

pending.description: A discovered recording with no store yet that is still expected to convert. Recorded rather than omitted so every raw recording is accounted for: before v3 these were silently absent from stores AND failures, which from outside is indistinguishable from 'still generating' forever (#1197).

reason.description: infra_failure: an untyped error (crashed worker, transient S3). memory_budget: it did not fit the memory free on the node at the time, which is a condition, not a property of the recording. not_attempted: this run did not reach it.

attempts.description: Conversion attempts so far. At 5 the producer promotes the entry to a failures[] entry with code retry_exhausted, so a permanently failing recording stops consuming the queue.

$comment: STABILITY POLICY. This schema is CLOSED at format_version 3: every object is additionalProperties:false, so a document carrying a field this schema does not name is invalid and the producer refuses to publish it. Additive change within v3 ships as format_version 3 with NEW OPTIONAL fields only, declared here -- a client pinned to v3 keeps validating. That is what `events_parquet`/`events_row_count` and `layout.events` are (#1060): optional, so an index for a dataset with no events -- and one written before they existed -- still validates, and `layout.events` is deliberately absent from layout's `required` set for the same reason. A BREAKING change (a removed or retyped field, a narrowed enum) is format_version 4 at a NEW schema path (/schemas/zarr-index-v4.json); this path keeps serving v3 for as long as any dataset publishes it, because the index is the mandatory entry point and a client cannot fall back to anything else. One reading rule changed inside v3 without a change of shape: a trial_types value longer than 128 code points is keyed by a 28-character digest form, and an index published before that change carries the literal value as its key (see that field). Read format_version before anything else.
